Auto Lock listing copy vs display engineering — two different jobs

US/EU indie teams conflate system screen-timeout settings with storefront language. iOS Settings and App Store Connect actually separate them:

  • Auto Lock on the device — under Settings → Display & Brightness → Auto-Lock, chooses how long the screen stays on before the iPhone locks: 30 Seconds, 1 Minute, 2 Minutes, 3 Minutes, 4 Minutes, 5 Minutes, or Never (自动锁定 / 自动锁屏). System behavior — outside AppLocale scope.
  • Keep-awake while using the app — some apps call UIApplication.shared.isIdleTimerDisabled or equivalent to prevent Auto Lock during navigation, video playback, or live sessions. Binary implementation — outside AppLocale scope. We rewrite how you describe that behavior on the store page.
  • Screen-timeout marketing on the product page — description paragraphs, subtitle positioning, keywords, promotional text, and screenshot overlays that tell buyers your app works best with longer Auto-Lock intervals, respects system timeout, or recommends Auto-Lock Never for hands-free use. Connect text fields — this page.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China storefront. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, and screenshot caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of how strongly your US listing markets Auto Lock compatibility.

An app that disables idle timer during a workout and a localized China listing are both valuable — neither replaces the other. AppLocale covers how you describe screen-timeout and keep-awake workflows on the store page, not whether isIdleTimerDisabled toggles inside your binary.

Auto Lock-specific listing vocabulary — what translates differently

Screen-timeout marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese buyers describe Auto Lock in iOS Settings — not a literal paste of US marketing:

Official Settings vocabulary

Apple's zh-Hans Settings UI uses 自动锁定 for Auto-Lock under 显示与亮度 (Display & Brightness), with related buyer language around 自动锁屏 (auto lock screen), 自动锁定时间 (auto-lock duration), 屏幕超时锁定 (screen timeout lock), and 自动锁屏时间 (auto lock screen time). Interval labels map to 30 秒, 1 分钟, 2 分钟, 5 分钟, and 永不 (Never). Listing copy should mirror that vocabulary — not generic 锁屏 that could mean Lock Screen wallpaper customization.

Auto Lock vs Tap to Wake — do not conflate

Auto Lock controls how long the bright screen stays on before locking. Tap to Wake controls whether tapping the screen wakes it from off when face-up — 轻点唤醒. zh-Hans listing copy should not imply 轻点唤醒 when your English source only showed an Auto-Lock interval picker. See the Tap to Wake listing guide only if tap-to-glance is your lead marketing claim.

Auto Lock vs Raise to Wake

Raise to Wake wakes the display when you lift the phone — 抬起唤醒. Auto Lock turns the display off after inactivity. Adjacent Display & Brightness settings with different buyer intent. See the Raise to Wake listing guide for lift-to-wake copy.

Auto Lock vs Always-On Display

Always-On Display keeps a dimmed lock screen visible while the phone rests — 全天候显示. Auto Lock times out the full bright screen. zh-Hans copy should not conflate them unless your English page explicitly markets both. See the Always-On Display listing guide for always-on dimming claims.

Auto Lock vs Low Power Mode

Low Power Mode may cap Auto-Lock at 30 seconds and reduce background activity — 低电量模式 under Settings → Battery. Your listing can mention both when accurate, but screen-timeout marketing and battery-saving compatibility are separate string families. See the Low Power Mode listing guide for 低电量模式 copy.

Keep-awake vs Auto-Lock Never tips

US pages often say "set Auto-Lock to Never" in onboarding tips while the app also disables idle timer in code. China storefront copy should describe the buyer benefit (屏幕使用期间保持常亮, 导航时屏幕不自动锁定) without implying AppLocale implements isIdleTimerDisabled — we rewrite listing strings only.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need timeout search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 自动锁定, 自动锁屏, and 屏幕常亮 each signal different intent from generic productivity keywords.

AppLocale FAQ

Is Auto Lock the same as Tap to Wake on the listing?

No. Auto Lock markets screen timeout and lock delay — 自动锁定, 自动锁屏, Settings → Display & Brightness → Auto-Lock. Tap to Wake markets tapping the screen to wake from off when face-up — 轻点唤醒. Different settings, different Connect string families. See our Tap to Wake listing guide for tap-to-glance copy.

Is Auto Lock the same as Raise to Wake?

No. Auto Lock controls how long the screen stays on before locking again. Raise to Wake controls whether lifting the phone wakes the display — 抬起唤醒. Adjacent Display & Brightness settings, separate listing copy. See our Raise to Wake listing guide for lift-to-wake copy.

Is Auto Lock the same as Always-On Display?

No. Auto Lock times out the full bright screen after inactivity. Always-On Display keeps a dimmed lock screen visible while the phone rests — 全天候显示. See our Always-On Display listing guide for always-on dimming copy.

Is Auto Lock the same as Low Power Mode?

No. Auto Lock is a Display & Brightness timeout — 自动锁定 under 显示与亮度. Low Power Mode is a Battery toggle that reduces background activity — 低电量模式. Listing copy for screen-timeout marketing is separate from battery-saving claims. See our Low Power Mode listing guide for 低电量模式 copy.
